title: Where to go for medical care: ER vs. urgent care vs. virtual care
summary: Compares emergency room, urgent care, virtual care, primary care and retail clinics and explains when to choose each.

Learn more about when to go to the ER

atoms.title: Five care options compared
atoms.question: What is the difference between urgent care, the ER, virtual care, a PCP and a retail clinic?
atoms.text: Urgent care is for issues that are not emergencies when your PCP is not available. The ER is for life-threatening and very serious conditions. Virtual care offers treatment from anywhere for minor medical and mental health care. A primary care provider (PCP) handles preventive and routine care. A retail or walk-in clinic provides quick treatment for minor illnesses or basic screenings.

atoms.title: Common conditions by care setting
atoms.question: What conditions are treated at urgent care versus the ER?
atoms.text: Urgent care commonly treats sprains, minor broken bones such as a finger, minor burns, minor infections, earache and strep throat. The ER handles heavy bleeding, chest pain, major burns, difficulty breathing, broken bones or spinal injuries, and progressive confusion or slurred speech. Retail clinics treat skin rash, routine vaccines, minor injuries, earache and sports physicals, and a PCP handles checkups and immunizations.

atoms.title: When to go to urgent care
atoms.question: When should I go to urgent care?
atoms.text: Urgent care treats illnesses and injuries that need care soon but are not emergencies, and can help when your PCP is away or cannot see you soon. It does not replace seeing your PCP. Urgent care may use simple lab tests such as urine tests, pregnancy tests or rapid strep tests, and may use X-rays. It typically lacks advanced tests such as CT scans or ultrasounds and may send you to an ER for more serious care.

atoms.title: When to go to the emergency room
atoms.question: When should I go to the ER?
atoms.text: ERs are for serious medical problems and are open 24 hours a day, every day of the year, with special equipment and trained doctors, physician assistants and nurses. For serious or life-threatening situations, call 911 or go to the nearest ER. If you are not sure you need an ambulance, call 911 and they can help you decide.

atoms.title: When you may need an ambulance
atoms.question: When do I need an ambulance?
atoms.text: You may need an ambulance if someone has chest pain, trouble breathing, sudden confusion or signs of a stroke; is choking, has stopped breathing or needs CPR; or had a car crash, fall or other accident and moving them could make the injury worse. In an emergency where you are unsure, call 911.

atoms.title: When to use virtual care
atoms.question: When is a virtual visit a good choice?
atoms.text: Virtual visits are a good choice if you do not need to see a provider in person. You can connect with a provider using your computer, tablet or smartphone, anytime and anywhere. Virtual visits can be a convenient way to get treatment options and even prescriptions for medications, if needed. For more serious problems, you may need to go to a clinic or hospital.

atoms.title: When to see your primary care provider
atoms.question: When should I see my primary care provider?
atoms.text: Your PCP is your go-to for routine checkups, preventive care and minor illnesses, and their in-depth knowledge of your health history makes them the best place to start. If you are ever unsure where to go, you can call your PCP, check your health plan's website or call the number on your health plan ID card to speak with an advocate.

atoms.title: When to go to a retail or walk-in clinic
atoms.question: When should I use a retail or walk-in clinic?
atoms.text: A retail or walk-in clinic is a good option for minor illnesses such as earaches or rashes. These clinics are typically staffed with nurse practitioners or physician assistants who can treat minor injuries, such as minor cuts or sprains, and give routine vaccines such as the flu shot. Student athletes can typically get a sports physical without an appointment. These clinics are typically faster and cheaper than urgent care or the ER.

atoms.title: Hours of availability by care option
atoms.question: Which care options are open outside regular office hours?
atoms.text: Urgent care, the emergency room, virtual care and retail or walk-in clinics are typically open 24/7, while a primary care provider is open during regular office hours and closed outside them. If you get sick after regular office hours, urgent care may be faster than waiting in a hospital emergency room.

atoms.title: Virtual visit service limitations
atoms.question: Are virtual visits meant for emergencies?
atoms.text: 24/7 Virtual Visits are not intended to address emergency or life-threatening medical conditions and should not be used in those circumstances. Unless otherwise required, benefits are available only when services are delivered through a Designated Virtual Network Provider. Services may not be available at all times, in all locations or for all members, so check your benefit plan.
